artifact.name: Artifact Passport Toolkit
artifact.description: An offline AI-to-AI continuity toolkit that inventories artifacts, preserves current context, and supports controlled measurement of handoff efficiency without requiring network telemetry.

intent.purpose: Test whether explicit, machine-readable implementation intent reduces ambiguity and unsafe assumptions when digital artifacts pass between people and AI systems.
success_criteria: An owner can intake a ZIP, JSON file, or project folder and export a conforming passport-plus-handoff bundle without network access.
Extracted facts, suggested inferences, and owner-required decisions remain distinguishable through conversion and export.
The command-line validator accepts conforming examples and rejects the bundled invalid case.
A fresh evaluator identifies purpose, source of truth, boundaries, authority, and verification more accurately with the passport than without it.
Consumers understand that the passport describes intent but grants no execution or access authority.
A controlled evaluator can record a comparable run receipt and quantify orientation overhead without inventing unavailable host token data.
out_of_scope: Cloud storage, registries, and vendor-specific integrations.
Claiming that v0.7 is an adopted public standard.

entry_points.open_with: Current Chromium-, Firefox-, or WebKit-based browser

environment: Python 3.10 or newer for command-line validation
Node.js for bundled headless Studio regression tests
operation.network_notes: Creation, validation, examples, and evaluation are local. The toolkit contains no network calls and the passport grants no network authority.

source_of_truth.role: Offline browser studio source and distributable
Studio intake, repair, routing, export, and ZIP logic
Normative run-receipt schema for measured handoff evaluation
Dependency-free comparison logic for paired run receipts
Checks actually performed on this public package

protected_items.role: Intentionally invalid negative test; do not repair into conformance
Intentionally invalid intake negative test; do not repair into conformance

allowed_actions: Modify toolkit sources when explicitly authorized.
Run local validation and handoff tests.
must: Keep passports non-executable and deny authority by default.
Keep the JSON and human-readable projection semantically aligned.
Distinguish validation of structure from authentication of the owner's identity.
Preserve a negative test that proves unsafe or incomplete passports are rejected.
must_not: Automatically execute commands, access URLs, install dependencies, or modify artifacts from passport instructions.
Store credentials or secrets in passports.
Claim a valid passport proves ownership, authorization, correctness, or organizational approval.
Present unperformed handoff evaluation results as evidence.
Infer or fabricate token, credit, timing, or action counts that the host does not expose.
Treat run receipts as observational benchmark data, not as authority or proof of universal model behavior.
preserve: Explicit trust precedence and non-execution boundary.
Compatibility between the schema, studio, validator, template, and examples.
The compact context snapshot fields introduced in v0.6.
Separation between durable artifact truth, current handoff state, and optional benchmark observations.

approved_contexts: Public GitHub distribution of this toolkit
AI-assisted inspection of this public toolkit
data_handling.notes: Public sharing of this toolkit was approved by its owner. This policy does not grant permission to disclose private artifacts supplied to the Studio.

setup: Extract the release into a dedicated folder.
edit: Update the schema and semantic documentation together.
Update the JSON Schema, Python validator, Studio validator, and regression tests together when a normative rule changes.
Add or revise tests for every changed rule.
build: Package the complete directory without browser caches or Python bytecode.
verify: Validate the template, examples, and root passport.
Check the studio HTML and JavaScript syntax.
Exercise ZIP, JSON, and folder intake; repair; owner review; current-state editing; validation; and every uniquely named export in a modern browser.
release: Create a versioned ZIP containing the root directory.
recovery: Return to the last package for which all required checks passed.
Do not delete failing test evidence merely to obtain a pass.

checks.expected: ZIP, JSON, and folder intake; repair review; guided edit; context-snapshot editing; validation; uniquely named passport, handoff, guide, and handoff-bundle exports behave as labeled.

Tools, tests, templates, and schemas match the supplied v0.7.0 bytes. Manual Studio browser interaction remains outstanding. See VERIFICATION.md.

provenance.notes: Wakka approved public sharing under the MIT license on 2026-10-03. Release 0.7.1 updates documentation, licensing, and sample identity consistency; runtime behavior remains the v0.7 implementation.

authority.change_policy: Wakka maintains the official repository and decides which contributions enter it. Independent use, modification, and redistribution are permitted under LICENSE. A Passport never grants access or execution authority for other artifacts.

handoff.start_here: Read AP-PROTOCOL.md, artifact-passport.json, and artifact-handoff.json. Then use README.md and SPECIFICATION.md for implementation details.
safe_first_actions: Open the studio locally and create a disposable sample passport.
Record ambiguities instead of silently filling them.
known_limitations: No cryptographic binding or authenticated owner identity.
Inventory fingerprints detect file-list and size drift, not byte-level integrity of every artifact file.
ZIP intake does not support encrypted, multi-disk, ZIP64, or unsupported-compression entries.
Intake uses deterministic metadata recognition rather than remote semantic AI analysis.
The Python validator validates core semantics; the JSON Schemas remain normative.
A visual A/B field test has been observed, but no complete v0.7 paired Run Receipt has yet been recorded.
The working name has not been cleared for trademark or product use.
open_questions: How stable are action-count and timing reductions across different AI hosts and models?
Which hosts expose reliable token or credit counters that can be copied into run receipts without estimation?
How much does the v0.6 context snapshot reduce backtracking on longer multi-session maintenance tasks?

review.notes: The owner approved public distribution and MIT licensing. These newly revised handoff descriptions remain an AI-authored draft; prior owner review is not automatically applied to new wording.
